labels.label: theo:universality_true
labels.notes: MARKED, and the mark is earned. I compared EGF.main_universality (Universality.lean:761) with main.tex:775 one clause at a time. (1) 'measured Polish space': any MeasurableSpace S, so weaker. [IsFiniteMeasure lam] is not an added hypothesis: it is the standing assumption 'a Polish space with a finite background measure' (l.161, also l.155), under which generative flows are defined. (2) 'pi a Markov kernel': [IsMarkovKernel pi], carried. (3) 'ergodic on (S, lambda)': dropped, which is weaker. (4) 'summable L2-mixing coefficients': IsSummablyL2Mixing pi lam, which is def:summably_mixing (see that row). (5) 'probability distributions F_init, F_term << lambda': carried. Their L2 densities are dropped, which is weaker. (6) Quantifiers: for all F_init, F_term, for all eps > 0, there exists f_out. Same as the paper. eps : ENNReal, and a real eps > 0 is covered through ENNReal.ofReal (checked by a probe). (7) Conclusion: f_out in L2(lambda) (MemLp fout 2 lam). The outflow is lam.withDensity (ofReal fout), the generative flow (pi, f_out lambda). initialError and terminalError are (F_term + F_out) - (F_init + F_out pi) and its mirror, Mathlib's truncated differences. For finite measures these are the Jordan negative and positive parts of F_init + F_in - F_term - F_out, exactly def:virtual_flows l.316 (initialError_eq_negPart and terminalError_eq_posPart, proved). The sum at Set.univ is < eps. On top of this the theorem gives f_out >= 0 and f_out bounded. Nonnegativity is needed anyway for (pi, f_out) to be a generative flow (l.161). Nothing is added, so 'stronger on both sides' is literally true. Proof spot-checked as a real proof. The case lamHat(S) = infinity is handled: gamma_0 < infinity forces lambda trivial (trivial_of_lamHat_univ_eq_top), so F_init = F_term and f_out = 0. Otherwise both laws are replaced by TV-close laws with density <= K and <= K dlamHat/dlam (exists_truncation). gamma_n -> 0 then gives TV-mixing (exists_tvMass_pushIter_lt): pushed parts stay below K lamHat, the space is split along {g < 1/m}, and e <= 1/k + k e^2 on the rest. The series is truncated at T and lifted by R = (T+1) K lamHat, which is invariant, so the lift costs nothing (tvMass_construction, an exact telescoping identity). Finally the outflow density is truncated at M. That makes 5 TV errors, each < eps/5. hsum is used only through gamma_0 != infinity (ENNReal.le_tsum 0) and gamma_n -> 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_atTop_zero_of_tsum_ne_top). Non-vacuity: main_universality_const instantiates the theorem through isSummablyL2Mixing_const, the resampling kernel pi(x) = lambda with lamHat = lambda (gamma_n = 0 for n >= 1, gamma_0 <= 1). That witness is genuine but it is not an EGF kernel, and it sits in the regime lamHat = lambda. No EGF kernel satisfying the hypothesis is built; that is S-egf-2's spectral-gap business and not required here.

labels.label: def:summably_mixing
labels.notes: MARKED. Taken as printed: invariant lamHat (lamHat.bind pi = lamHat) equivalent to lambda (both <<); lamHat any measure, as printed. H = {MemLp phi 2 lam, eLpNorm phi 2 lam = 1, integral phi d lam = 0}. gamma_n = sup over H of the lintegral of ofReal((phi pi^n)^2) against lamHat, in [0, infinity]. tsum != infinity. The two points the closer calls 'fixed by the paper's own text' are both printed at l.273, in the paragraph that explains this very property. That paragraph names the operator pi induces on L2, phi -> d((phi lambda)pi)/d lambda, and the subspace {phi : integral phi d lambda = 0}. The proof (l.788-789: eps_t(S) = 0, d eps_t/d lambda) uses both. The paper's notation agrees: mu pi is the image measure (l.158), and f_in = d(F_out pi)/d lambda (l.196). No alternative operator is printed anywhere. So this is the paper's text, not a free reading, and I accept the mark (and through it the headline's). The transfer as defined (rnDeriv of the pushed phi+ lambda and phi- lambda) agrees a.e. with the n-th iterate of the one-step operator: everything pushed stays << lamHat << lambda. lambda is finite in the theorem, so the Bochner-integral junk convention (a non-integrable phi with 'integral 0') never enters. Caveat, raised as minor finding 1: l.273 is a sufficient-condition remark. The paper's only use of the definition (the proof) works with lamHat = lambda. In that regime the lambda-transfer, the lamHat-transfer and the Markov operator on functions all give the same gamma_n. When lamHat != lambda they differ, and neither summability implies the other. The REPORT should carry a confirmation question; the closer itself records that the definition does not agree with how it is used (H in L2(lambda), gamma_n against lamHat, proof against lambda). Its three findings are true: no measure at l.267; lamHat vs lambda; inhabitation.

labels.label: def:egf
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial. The question is legitimate. IsEGF takes the forward-word 'that is' clause, foldl applying Phi_{i1} first (the right action of l.221). IsTopologicallyErgodic.group shows the clause implies the group version. shiftZ_group_not_forward is valid: on discrete Z the group of n -> n+1 has every orbit equal to Z, while forward words from 0 never reach the open set {-1}. So the clause is strictly stronger, and is not Lean >= paper under the group reading, which is why the row stays unmarked. isTopologicallyErgodic_iff_pos is correct (t = 0 is immaterial for p >= 1). For p = 0 no EGF exists anyway, because the weights cannot sum to 1. Moving from manifolds and diffeomorphisms to topological measurable spaces and measurable homeomorphisms is a generalisation (Diffeomorph.toHomeomorph; Borel). Two wording points are in minor finding 4: the measurability of alpha is not 'forced', and the R^d remark. The roadmap's evidence for this generalisation is as the closer reports.

labels.label: def:universal_family
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial, and both questions are real. IsUniversalFamily quantifies over probability measures mu, nu << lambda with ess-bounded rnDeriv. It asks for some F in the family with exact flow matching nu + F_out pi = mu + F_out (l.183, l.251). A Lean family is any Set (GenerativeFlow S), and the outflows need not have densities. Every paper family (outflows f_out lambda) is such a set, so the definition specialises correctly. not_isUniversalFamilyUnnormalized is valid. Mass is conserved because the kernel is Markov, so nu = lambda, mu = 2 lambda would force lambda(S) = 2 lambda(S), and lambda is finite and nonzero. That is also the first claim of theo:sampling_theorem. The l.774 finding is true. theo:universality_true gives only an eps-defect, and exact universality does not follow from it plus density of the f_out. A family whose f_out range over a countable dense set, with one kernel, matches only countably many differences F_term - F_init, so even the implication's conclusion can fail as printed. The l.277 finding is true: the non-negative cone is closed in L2, so it is not dense.

findings.where: scaffold/EGFScaffold/Defs.lean:87-92 (SCOPE), 340-359 (transfer, unitMeanZero, IsSummablyL2Mixing); REPORT row def:summably_mixing ('questions': [])
findings.what: The two fill-ins of def:summably_mixing are accepted as the paper's text. These are phi pi^n := d((phi lambda)pi^n)/d lambda, and mean zero against lambda. Both are printed at l.273, and the marks stand. But they come from a sufficient-condition remark, not from the definition. The paper's only use of the definition (the proof, l.788-789) works with lamHat = lambda. In that regime the lambda-transfer, the lamHat-transfer d((phi lamHat)pi^n)/d lamHat (with integral phi d lamHat = 0) and the Markov operator phi -> integral phi(y) pi^n(s, dy) all give the same gamma_n, because they have adjoint operator norms on the mean-zero subspace. When lamHat != lambda they differ, and neither summability implies the other. So the paper's evidence cannot tell them apart where it matters. The definition is also internally inconsistent, as the closer itself records. kb/0011 asks that such a choice be reported as a question even when it is disclosed in SCOPE. If the author ever rules the lamHat version, both marks (def:summably_mixing, and theo:universality_true through it) have to be re-proved.
findings.fix: Add a confirmation question to the def:summably_mixing row. When lamHat != lambda, is phi pi^n the operator of l.273, d((phi lambda)pi^n)/d lambda, with integral phi d lambda = 0 (taken)? Or the transfer in L2(lamHat)? Note that both marks rest on the answer. No Lean change is needed now.

findings.where: REPORT theo:universality_true findings[0] and [1], hypotheses row 'pi ergodic on (S, lambda)' ('the proof never uses it'); Universality.lean:67-70 (Findings 1-2)
findings.what: Finding 2 is true clause by clause: l.793 uses lambda pi = lambda, l.779 uses that pi preserves L2(lambda) densities, and def:summably_mixing provides only an invariant lamHat. It is incomplete, though. 'pi is ergodic on (S, lambda)' in Walters' sense, which the paper cites at l.211 ('0-flows are measures xi for which pi is ergodic', invariant measures), is a statement about a pi-invariant lambda. l.819 applies the master theorem right after noting 'each Phi_i keep the Lebesgue measure lambda invariant'. Under that reading, l.779 (by Jensen, the transfer contracts L2(lambda) when lambda is invariant) and l.793 are justified by the theorem's own hypothesis, and the paper's proof does use (that part of) ergodicity. Sent as it stands, the finding presents as a gap something the author can close by pointing at 'ergodic'. Its true content is that the Lean theorem needs neither the invariance of lambda nor ergodicity. Relatedly, gamma_n -> 0 with gamma_0 < infinity already forces (pi, lamHat) to be ergodic. Sketch: an invariant set A with 0 < lamHat(A) < lamHat(S) gives phi = (1_A - c) dlamHat/dlam, which is in L2(lambda) because gamma_0 < infinity forces dlamHat/dlam to be essentially bounded, and phi pi^n = phi for all n. So 'without ergodicity' (finding 1) is cosmetic, except for the invariance of lambda.
findings.fix: Reword finding 2 as follows. If 'ergodic on (S, lambda)' includes the invariance of lambda (Walters; l.211, l.819), then l.779 and l.793 are justified, and the Lean theorem drops that invariance. If it does not, they are gaps. In finding 1 say that ergodicity is implied by the mixing hypothesis, and that the invariance of lambda is what is genuinely dropped. In the hypothesis note, 'the proof never uses it' should read 'the Lean proof never uses it'.

findings.what: The criticism of l.789 is right as written. 'Summable squared norms, therefore nu_T converges' is a non-sequitur, and |nu_inf|_2 <= sum of squared norms mixes norms and squares. Two points are overstated. First, '(that needs sum ||d eps_t/d lambda||_2 < infinity)': absolute summability is sufficient, not necessary. Second, the finding does not say that the conclusion is recoverable in one line in the regime the proof works in (lamHat = lambda, lambda invariant). There gamma_n is a supremum, gamma_n = ||T^n restricted to H0||^2, with T the transfer, a contraction of L2(lambda) preserving H0 = {integral phi d lambda = 0}. So sum gamma_n < infinity gives ||T^N on H0|| <= 1/2 for some N, hence geometric decay and absolute convergence of sum eps_t in L2(lambda). The genuine obstruction is only the lamHat != lambda mismatch, which the finding already names. As it stands it would reach the author as 'the convergence step fails', when the argument fails and the conclusion does not.
findings.fix: Replace 'that needs' with 'that would follow from'. Add that for lamHat = lambda the step is repaired by the submultiplicativity of the sup-defined gamma_n. Keep the lamHat-vs-lambda clause as the real gap.

findings.where: REPORT def:egf findings[1] and hypotheses row 'policy alpha'; Defs.lean:81 (checklist); REPORT def:egf findings[0] ('The same happens for translations of R^d')
findings.what: (a) That the weights sum to 1 is forced by pi being Markov. That alpha is measurable is not. Take Phi_1 = Phi_2 = id, alpha_1 = 1_N with N non-measurable, and alpha_2 = 1 - alpha_1: this gives the measurable identity kernel. Add Phi_3 an irrational rotation (weights halved) and it is even topologically ergodic. On a standard Borel space a measurable alpha' with the same pi always exists, so the condition is harmless as an existential. But IsEGF takes alpha as a parameter, so it is a mild added condition on a partial row, not a consequence. (b) 'The same happens for translations of R^d' holds for some families (+1, +sqrt 2 on R: the group orbits are dense, the forward orbits lie in [x, infinity)) but not for all (+1, -sqrt 2 has dense forward orbits). Also, Z and R^d carry infinite volume, outside the finite-lambda standing assumption of l.161, although the clause being compared is purely topological.
findings.fix: (a) Say that measurability is a mild condition, assumed without loss of generality on standard Borel spaces (or supported by l.288's softmax head), rather than 'forced'. (b) Say 'can happen for translations of R^d (e.g. +1, +sqrt 2 on R)'.
